To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the consultation process was the key factor in determining public acceptability; (2) the consultation process is the most important factor in determining public support for schemes; (3) the consultation process should be as open and transparent as possible; (4) the consultation process must be seen to be open and transparent; (5) consultation must be carried out in a timely manner and be responsive to public opinion; (6) the public must be given sufficient information to make an informed choice;

'The consultation process is the key determinant of success of a traffic calming scheme, in that the more the public feel they have been involved in a process of consultation, the greater their acceptance of a scheme'.

consultation is an essential component of successful schemes; that the most successful schemes were those in which the consultation process was most open and in which the local community was given the most information; and that the most effective methods of consultation were the most informal.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the most successful traffic calming schemes are those where the local community is fully involved and where there is a clear and open dialogue between the local residents and the council.
consultation is a key part of traffic calming schemes and that the process of consultation needs to be open and inclusive.
the more consultation, the better, but that it must be done well.
The main takeaway from our work is that
consultation is not just a matter of 'doing it' but a matter of doing it well.
consultation is not an end in itself, but is part of a process of building trust and confidence between the local authority and the community.
, in order to be successful, consultation should be a two-way process, with the council listening to the public as well as the public listening to the council.
